letters.desc: Constellation argues that resource adequacy concerns should be addressed through improved load forecasting, voluntary demand response products, and market-based reliability backstop enhancements rather than discriminatory conditions on large load interconnection. The Enhanced Backstop proposal targets incremental capacity under tight market conditions without suppressing price signals.
quotes: Discrimination against existing generation resources will undermine resource adequacy by signaling that existing capacity is less valuable than new capacity in serving load, even when existing capacity can serve load more efficiently.

The Commission should let existing market mechanisms work to ensure resource adequacy. If it determines that reform is needed, it should adopt competitive market fixes that preserve market-based incentives for capital investment, such as the Joint Stakeholders' Reliability Backstop Alternative

letters.desc: ODEC calls for any transition plan to explicitly address resource adequacy, requiring that capacity be in place before large loads interconnect, and shielding existing consumers from cost impacts through hedging or other mechanisms.
quotes: Any transition plan must address resource adequacy for both system stability and consumer costs.

letters.desc: ODEC warns that large load interconnections involving generator suspension threaten resource adequacy for existing customers who have financially supported those generators. ODEC calls for FERC to exercise its full authority and clarify federal and state roles in preserving resource adequacy.
quotes: the Final Rule should recognize that interconnecting large loads that will result in partial or full suspension of an existing resource raises different and more concerning impacts than a load interconnection with a build-your-own generation arrangement that includes new generation.
The former arrangement will siphon resources away from the very loads that have financially supported the existing generation, at a time when resource adequacy is already severely threatened.

letters.org: Pennsylvania Office of Consumer AdvocateDelaware Division of the Public Advocate
letters.desc: The filers support interconnecting large loads and hybrid facilities only when they bring or procure sufficient capacity to offset their addition to grid load, whether through on-site generation, reserves, or capacity-backed demand response.
quotes: The Joint Consumer Advocates support large loads and hybrid facilities that interconnect to the system only if they bring sufficient capacity (either through generation and reserves or capacity-backed demand response) to offset the additional load brought onto the grid.

letters.desc: SPP argues that any new load, including curtailable load, requires corresponding generation capacity and energy. SPP warns against prioritizing non-firm load over load backed by Designated Resources, and references NERC's energy assurance standards work.
quotes: Any load connected to the SPP Transmission System, including load that agrees to be curtailed, will require energy to be produced and will take some capacity from the Transmission System; otherwise, they would not need to connect to the grid. Even when agreeing to curtail, a curtailable, or non-firm load, will impact existing and future firm load and should not be prioritized over a load that is willing to bring, or already has Designated Resources.

letters.desc: TAPS urges that the SSR/RMR study for co-located arrangements include resource adequacy and capacity market analysis, and that results be made public so regulators and stakeholders can evaluate whether additional steps are needed to maintain affordability.
quotes: the unique size and accelerated timing of new large data center loads, coupled with existing resource adequacy challenges (given retirements of generation and generation interconnection queue backlogs creating barriers to their timely replacement), make it vital to understand the resource adequacy and capacity market implications of taking generation that now serves regional load and instead sequestering it to exclusively serve a co-located large data center load.

letters.org: Utility Intervention Unit, New York State Department of Stat
letters.desc: The UIU warns that large flexible loads can distort resource adequacy planning and that generators retreating behind the meter to serve dedicated large loads could create capacity shortfalls. It calls for forward-looking RMR-type studies and a no-adverse-impact standard before any BTM arrangement is approved.
quotes: In no instance should existing load customers be on the hook for increased capacity costs (this includes the cost of RMR-style contracts) because a generator has decided to exit the market to serve a large load BTM.

letters.org: New York Independent System Operator, Inc.
letters.desc: NYISO emphasizes that large load additions can stress resource adequacy even without co-location, and that New York already faces shrinking reliability margins. It flags this as a gap in the ANOPR principles and calls for any rule to address resource adequacy impacts of large loads broadly.
quotes: the current fleet of generating resources connected to the New York Control Area ("NYCA") is decreasing while insufficient generation with the necessary characteristics is entering service.
it is important to note that resource adequacy issues can also arise when large loads are added to the system, unrelated to a proposal to co-locate with an existing generator.

letters.desc: OPSI warns that if large loads interconnect faster than new generation comes online, resource adequacy obligations become unclear, and the Commission must clarify who bears those obligations in both restructured and vertically integrated contexts.
quotes: The Commission should clarify who is responsible for meeting resource adequacy and reliability obligations in both restructured and vertically integrated contexts.

letters.org: PSEG CompaniesPSEG Energy Resources & Trade LLCPSEG Power LLC ,Public Service Electric and Gas Company ,
letters.desc: PSEG describes a looming resource adequacy crisis in PJM, where aging thermal generation is retiring while load growth accelerates. It calls for an all-of-the-above strategy including improved load forecasting, state-sponsored generation, and an expedited interconnection track.
quotes: large loads should not create or exacerbate the resource adequacy problem that exists in many parts of the country.
it is necessary to implement an 'all-of-the-above' approach that includes bringing significant amounts of new generation supply on-line as soon as possible.
it would be inappropriate to consider resource adequacy issues in the study process for co-located load/hybrid arrangements.

letters.desc: Talen frames sufficient generation to meet forecasted demand growth as the underlying problem that large load interconnection rules alone will not solve.
quotes: The way to ensure all loads are reliably served is by ensuring there are sufficient generation resources to meet the forecasted exponential growth in demand.
